name: Small-carrier trucking insurance brokerage through an existing carrier/driver network
thesis: Build a focused commercial P&C brokerage for Chicago-area 1-10 truck operators, using the owner’s existing small-carrier/driver network as the qualifying initial distribution edge. The business earns commissions on large recurring insurance spend and compounds only if renewals/retention and market access are strong.

producer_path.use: lower-capital future validation path after licensing; not evidence of our own contract
producer_path.evidence: current trucking producer program pays 50% new and 50% renewal agency commission while agency supplies software/x-dates

known_cost_exclusions: bond if required by placement model

includes: business-entity fee only in entity scenario
known_first_year_fixed_floor.interpretation: fixed-cost coverage arithmetic only; not profit forecast

stress_case_research_feasibility.purpose: research feasibility stress-test only; empirical net contribution remains a market-validation gate

acquisition_strategy.primary: existing owner-confirmed network of roughly 40 driver/carrier prospects
acquisition_strategy.conditional_future: repair/service-center embedded placement only after access is revalidated/formalized

two_person_plan.phase_1: one licensed producer plus founder-operated intake/quoting/admin
two_person_plan.constraint: no sales before licensing/market access; owner time must be measured per quote and renewal

scale_path.phase_2: CSR/account manager when renewal book supports payroll
scale_path.phase_3: additional producer or replicated trucking-service/referral channels only after one channel’s economics are proven

risks: local trucking-insurance competition is strong
carrier/MGA access can determine whether quotes are competitive
one major Great West referral route excludes the seven Chicagoland counties
licensing/E&O/bond/agency compliance add fixed and operating cost
the 40-prospect network may not convert or may decay
truck accounts can be service-intensive and cancellation-sensitive
unknowns: Exact weekly qualified traffic and current-policy renewal calendar are unknown.
Bind rate from repair/service referrals is unknown.
Carrier/MGA access for new trucking risks and new ventures must be verified contractually.
Net commission after aggregator/MGA splits and service workload must be modeled.
Illinois producer/entity licensing and any agency registration requirements must be completed before selling.
Retention and remarketing workload for small trucking accounts is unknown.
kill_conditions: If embedded channel produces fewer than 5 qualified trucking insurance conversations per month after launch.
If market-access partners cannot place the dominant local risk profiles competitively.
If net first-year commission after splits/service cost is too low to support the sales and servicing workload.
If annual retention is weak enough that renewal economics do not compound.
If repair-shop access cannot be formalized or becomes non-exclusive/low-quality traffic.

feedback_state.interpretation: Passed all research gates; requires separate owner-approved market validation before winner status.

name: Small-carrier repair/equipment/working-capital referral desk through an existing carrier network
thesis: Use the owner-confirmed small-carrier/driver network to route qualified repair, equipment, factoring and working-capital needs to vetted third-party providers. Revenue comes from referral/rev-share economics; the business is attractive only if annual revenue per network contact materially exceeds relationship/admin cost.

business_model.delivery: qualified handoff to third-party licensed/finance providers
revenue_units: possible residual/rev share depending on partner
explicit_non_thesis: building a loan marketplace before proving channel economics

economics_summary.interpretation: economics can be very low-touch but are materially smaller per customer than insurance brokerage unless residual factoring or higher-value finance compensation is secured

acquisition_strategy.primary: same owner-confirmed trucking network used by OPP-V5-01-A
acquisition_strategy.trigger: major repair, equipment need, working-capital/factoring pain

two_person_plan.phase_1: one person can qualify and route leads using partner portals
two_person_plan.compliance: referral compensation and disclosures must follow applicable law/partner terms
two_person_plan.service_burden: low after handoff if partner owns underwriting/servicing

scale_path.phase_2: add more vetted finance/protection partners only where buyer need and compensation are measured
scale_path.phase_3: replicate through additional repair/service partners if referral attribution and economics remain positive

risks: low per-deal referral fees can cap revenue
partner owns underwriting and often the customer economics
attribution and payout terms vary
financial-product referral rules can vary by product/state
buyer trust can be damaged by poor partner outcomes
not all repair events create finance demand
unknowns: qualified finance/referral conversations per month
funding/close rate by partner
average payout and payout timing
residual vs one-time compensation
customer consent/compliance requirements
partner quality/default/complaint risk
kill_conditions: If realized revenue per qualified lead is too small to justify attention.
If fewer than 10% of qualified network contacts create a finance/protection referral opportunity over 12 months.
If partner complaints/default outcomes damage the core trucking network relationship.

feedback_state.reason: At the evidenced ~40-contact channel scale, verified referral payouts are too small/irregular for a standalone business. Keep as possible ancillary monetization only if another trucking business already owns the customer relationship.

name: Managed DOT compliance subscription for small trucking fleets through the existing carrier/driver network
thesis: Operate a focused recurring compliance desk for 1–10 truck carriers, combining DQ/renewal/deadline/audit-readiness administration with third-party testing/MVR/Clearinghouse infrastructure where appropriate. Initial acquisition comes from the owner-confirmed trucking network, not from paid leads.

secondary: ancillary partner referrals only if compliant

economics_summary.interpretation: Revenue arithmetic only; no labor-adjusted profit forecast until service workload is measured.
economics_summary.research_gate_status: unit economics structurally feasible; actual net contribution remains empirical

acquisition_strategy.primary: existing owner-confirmed network of roughly 40 driver/carrier prospects
acquisition_strategy.conditional_future: repair/service-center distribution only after access is refreshed/formalized

two_person_plan.phase_1: one founder handles sales/account intake while the second person/admin stack handles recurring document/deadline workflow; testing/MVR backend may be partnered
two_person_plan.constraint: Do not claim two-person feasibility until monthly service minutes and exception workload are bounded

scale_path.phase_2: standardized SOPs and compliance-management platform for a larger book
scale_path.phase_3: dedicated compliance account manager/CSR when recurring MRR supports payroll; expand through partner/referral channels only after retention and CAC evidence

risks: strong Chicago/national compliance competition
low-price software and managed substitutes compress pricing
regulatory mistakes can create customer harm and liability
service labor may scale poorly
customer documents contain sensitive business/driver data and require strong security
warm network may not convert
unknowns: Actual service minutes per account and monthly workload are unmeasured.
Professional-liability/general-liability needs and exact scope disclaimers must be verified before launch.
Current network willingness to outsource compliance administration is unmeasured.
Retention/churn and support intensity are unknown.
Economics of testing/MVR/Clearinghouse/vendor pass-through must be modeled precisely.
Scale beyond the initial network must not depend on paid leads until CAC is measured.
kill_conditions: Reject if routine recurring service cannot be standardized to roughly <=2 owner-hours/account/month at realistic realized pricing.
Reject if onboarding/exception labor or liability/security cost removes positive labor-adjusted contribution.
Reject if low-cost substitutes force realized price below a sustainable level.
Reject if the warm network fails to produce qualified compliance conversations in a future approved test.
Reject if liability exposure cannot be bounded with SOPs, insurance and clear scope.
Reject if founder labor cannot transition to repeatable account-management workflows.

feedback_state.interpretation: All research gates passed; winner status requires owner-approved measured channel response, CAC and net contribution.

name: Trucking bookkeeping subscription through the existing carrier/driver network
thesis: Provide a bounded monthly bookkeeping/financial back-office service for 1-10 truck carriers: reconciliations, trucking-specific categorization, settlement/factoring review, truck-level P&L and CPA-ready books. Tax-return preparation, CPA titles and assurance work are excluded from launch scope.

explicit_non_thesis: generic SMB bookkeeping without trucking-specific workflow

economics_summary.research_gate_status: unit economics and two-person capacity structurally feasible; actual net contribution remains empirical

acquisition_strategy.future: referrals and public carrier prospecting only after measured CAC/retention

two_person_plan.phase_1: founder intake plus standardized monthly-close workflow
two_person_plan.constraint: do not pass two-person gate until recurring and cleanup hours/account are bounded

scale_path.phase_2: dedicated bookkeeper when book supports payroll
scale_path.phase_3: review lead/controller and compliant tax/CPA partner channel if customer demand supports it

risks: crowded category with low-price substitutes
bookkeeping errors can damage customer decisions/tax handoff
catch-up cleanup can create large one-time labor
financial data security/privacy
customers may expect tax advice outside scope
warm network may not convert
unknowns: Actual monthly transaction volume and service hours by 1-truck vs 2-10-truck account are unknown.
Software/client-file cost per account is unmodeled.
Catch-up/cleanup labor can be much larger than recurring monthly close.
Actual network willingness to outsource bookkeeping is unmeasured.
Bookkeeping quality-control/review process must be defined.
Tax-return preparation, tax advice, attest/assurance and CPA-title use must remain out of launch scope unless proper credentials/requirements are satisfied.
Retention/churn is unknown.
kill_conditions: Reject if full managed recurring price is materially below ~$350/account without a correspondingly lighter scope.
Reject if routine recurring service exceeds roughly 5 hours/account/month at ~$350 realized price after workflow stabilization.
Reject if cleanup/catch-up cannot be separately priced and scheduled.
Reject if the warm network produces no qualified bookkeeping demand in a future approved test.
Reject if QA/review requires founder-only accounting expertise that cannot be standardized or hired.
Reject if customers primarily demand regulated tax/CPA/assurance services outside the bounded launch scope.

feedback_state.interpretation: All research gates passed/not-applicable; winner status requires owner-approved measured response, CAC and net contribution.
